claims.claim: pumpkinseed minimally active at ≤ 7.9 °C and fasting at ≤ 4 °C
claims.location: web page, Results, 'Experiment 1: Behavioural responses to cooling to winter temperature', 3rd paragraph
claims.quote: Pumpkinseed, however, exhibited more dissimilar inactive and fasting steady states (≤7.9°C and ≤4.0°C
claims.conditions: laboratory, adults from Lily Lake, Saint John, New Brunswick (n = 12); cooled ~1 °C a day from 14 °C to ~2 °C; daytime cold steady states (temperatures at which a behaviour no longer differed from its value at the coldest temperature); ration ~0.5 % body mass a day
claims.note: both are 'steady states', not complete inactivity or fasting: 'pumpkinseed never reached inactivity' and some fed a little at the coldest temperature (Discussion, 'Pumpkinseed sunfish')

claims.claim: pumpkinseed cooled to about 2.5 °C were minimally active at ≤ 7.9 °C and stopped feeding at ≤ 4 °C
claims.source_value: in the behaviour experiment (cooling ~1 °C a day from 14 °C to ~2 °C) the minimally active steady state began at 7.9 °C and the fasting steady state at ≤ 4.0 °C; feeding fell steeply below 7.9 °C, 'by 2.2°C all but one pumpkinseed had ceased feeding', and certain individuals kept feeding at a low level at the coldest temperature; the ~2.5 °C is the respirometry experiment (4–6 weeks' acclimation), which measured activity and metabolism, not feeding
claims.location: web page, Results (Experiment 1, 2nd–3rd paragraphs); Discussion, 'Pumpkinseed sunfish'
claims.quote: certain individuals continued to feed at a low level even at the coldest temperature
claims.conditions: laboratory, n = 12, acute cooling at ~1 °C a day; 24 h at each temperature
claims.note: suggested wording: 'cooled ~1 °C a day to ~2 °C, pumpkinseed reached a minimally active state at 7.9 °C and a near-fasting state at ≤ 4 °C, though some still fed a little'

claims.claim: no metabolic depression beyond the ordinary temperature effect
claims.location: web page, Results (Experiment 2: thermal sensitivity of SMR) and Discussion
claims.quote: in mummichog and pumpkinseed (though their average Q 10 were <3.5)
claims.conditions: respirometry with video-tracked activity; acute cooling ~3 °C a day from ~14 °C to ~2.5 °C, then 4–6 weeks at ~2.5 °C; SMR = metabolic rate extrapolated to zero activity; MRD defined as Q10 > 3.5 (n = 11 pumpkinseed)
claims.note: mean SMR Q10 < 3.5 in every interval, a few individuals above; routine (activity-uncontrolled) Q10 reached 5.6 in pumpkinseed

claims.claim: pumpkinseed are lethargic but not dormant in winter
claims.location: web page, Discussion, 'The classification of overwintering strategies in fishes'
claims.quote: pumpkinseed and mummichog are examples of winter-lethargic species, rather than winter dormant as previously reported
claims.conditions: laboratory classification from the behaviour and respirometry experiments

claims.quote: zero or near zero activity was recorded at and below 7.1°C and 7.9°C, respectively
claims.conditions: daytime spontaneous activity in individual arenas with a shelter, laboratory (the 7.9 °C is pumpkinseed's; 7.1 °C cunner's)

notes: The fish were New Brunswick pumpkinseed (Lily Lake), a good regional match for Maine. Activity Q10 from 14 to 8 °C was 267 ± 122 by day in pumpkinseed (Discussion) — the behavioural shutdown is steep. Cold steady states were analysed by day only for this diurnal species. The paper's MRD verdict rests on SMR Q10 < 3.5; earlier reports of Q10 6.0 for cooled pumpkinseed (Roberts 1964) are attributed to uncontrolled activity. The only correction is wording: 'stopped feeding' should be a near-fasting steady state, and the 'cooled to about 2.5 °C' belongs to the metabolic experiment, not the feeding thresholds.
